items.en: Have you seen what's going on with
items.example: Have you seen what's going on with the trains this week?
items.exampleTr: Bu hafta trenlerde olanları gördün mü?
items.simple: A way to start talking about some news you want to discuss.
dialogue: A: Have you seen what's going on with the petrol prices?
B: I know! I nearly cried at the pump.
items.note: Haber/dedikodu sohbetini açmanın en doğal yolu.

items.en: I'll believe it when I see it
items.example: They say the new road will open in May. I'll believe it when I see it.
items.exampleTr: Yeni yolun mayısta açılacağını söylüyorlar. Görmeden inanmam.
items.simple: You don't trust a promise until it really happens.
dialogue: A: The landlord says he'll fix the heating this week.
B: I'll believe it when I see it.
items.note: Siyasi vaatler, tamirci sözleri için alaycı.

items.example: The way I see it, they should have resigned weeks ago.
items.exampleTr: Bana kalırsa haftalar önce istifa etmeleri gerekirdi.
items.simple: Words you say before you tell your own idea about something.
dialogue: A: Do you think the strike will work?
B: The way I see it, they've got nothing to lose.
items.note: Görüş bildirmeye başlarken; 'In my opinion'dan daha sohbet dili.

items.en: I'm not one for gossip, but
items.example: I'm not one for gossip, but guess who's leaving?
items.exampleTr: Dedikoduyu sevmem ama bil bakalım kim ayrılıyor?
items.simple: Something people say right before they share some gossip.
dialogue: A: I'm not one for gossip, but did you hear about Dan and Lucy?
B: No! Tell me everything.
items.note: Esprili ikiyüzlülük: bunu diyen hemen dedikodu yapar.

items.example: Word on the street is they're closing the Leeds office.
items.exampleTr: Söylentiye göre Leeds ofisini kapatıyorlar.
items.simple: People are saying this, but nobody is sure it's true.
dialogue: A: Any news about the restructure?
B: Word on the street is it's happening in March.
items.note: Gayriresmî, hafif esprili; 'Rumour has it' ile yakın.

items.example: The minister got caught speeding on his way to a road safety talk. You couldn't make it up.
items.exampleTr: Bakan, trafik güvenliği konuşmasına giderken hız yaparken yakalandı. Uydursan bu kadar olmaz.
items.simple: Something is so silly or strange that nobody could invent it.
dialogue: A: The fire station burned down last night.
B: Seriously? You couldn't make it up.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; absürt haberler için.

items.example: Who'd have thought he'd end up running the company?
items.exampleTr: Kim derdi onun şirketi yöneteceğini?
items.simple: You are surprised, because nobody expected this.
dialogue: A: Tom from accounts is getting married.
B: Who'd have thought it? He never talks to anyone.
items.note: Bazen tek başına: 'Who'd have thought it?'

items.example: Call me cynical, but I think they only did it for the publicity.
items.exampleTr: Bana kuşkucu de ama bence sırf reklam için yaptılar.
items.simple: You say this before a doubtful idea, so people don't think you're too negative.
dialogue: A: The company's donating to charity now.
B: Call me cynical, but it's tax time.
items.note: 'Call me old-fashioned, but' de aynı yapıda.

items.en: I wouldn't put it past him
items.example: Did he really lie about that? I wouldn't put it past him.
items.exampleTr: Gerçekten bu konuda yalan mı söyledi? Ondan her şey beklenir.
items.simple: You think he might do a bad thing, because that's what he's like.
dialogue: A: Do you think Gary took the last biscuit?
B: I wouldn't put it past him.
items.note: Zamir değişir: 'I wouldn't put it past her/them.'

items.en: Sounds a bit fishy to me
items.example: A free holiday just for answering a call? Sounds a bit fishy to me.
items.exampleTr: Sadece telefona cevap verdin diye bedava tatil mi? Bana biraz şüpheli geliyor.
items.simple: Something seems not quite right, maybe a trick.
dialogue: A: He says he lost the receipt and the box.
B: Sounds a bit fishy to me.
items.note: 'fishy' = kokuşmuş, şüpheli.

items.example: Their argument at the party is the talk of the office.
items.exampleTr: Partideki kavgaları ofiste herkesin dilinde.
items.simple: Something everyone at work is talking about.
dialogue: A: Why is everyone whispering?
B: Your new haircut is the talk of the office!
items.note: 'the talk of the town' kalıbından; yer değişebilir.

items.tr: bu hiç hoş görünmüyor, imaj açısından kötü
items.example: Posting party pics on a sick day? That's not a good look.
items.exampleTr: Hastalık izninde parti fotoğrafı paylaşmak mı? Bu hiç hoş görünmüyor.
items.simple: What someone did makes them look bad to other people.
dialogue: A: The CEO got a bonus while cutting jobs.
B: That's not a good look.
items.note: Yeni ve çok yaygın; ünlüler ve şirketler için.

items.en: Let's not go down that road
items.example: Politics at Christmas dinner? Let's not go down that road.
items.exampleTr: Yılbaşı yemeğinde siyaset mi? O konuya hiç girmeyelim.
items.simple: Let's not start talking about that, it will only cause trouble.
dialogue: A: So, who did you vote for?
B: Let's not go down that road.
items.note: Tartışma çıkaracak konuyu kibarca kapatmak için.

items.example: He was seen at the hotel with someone else? The plot thickens.
items.exampleTr: Otelde başka biriyle mi görülmüş? Olay derinleşiyor.
items.simple: The story is getting more interesting and mysterious.
dialogue: A: And then she deleted all her photos with him.
B: Ooh, the plot thickens.
items.note: Esprili; dedikodu ya da gizem gibi bir durumda.

items.example: There's a video doing the rounds of the boss dancing.
items.exampleTr: Patronun dans ettiği bir video elden ele dolaşıyor.
items.simple: A story, joke or illness that goes from person to person.
dialogue: A: Have you heard the rumour about the merger?
B: Yeah, it's been doing the rounds all week.
items.note: Söylenti, video, grip için: 'There's a bug doing the rounds.'

items.en: Make of that what you will
items.example: He said he was 'busy' on Saturday. Make of that what you will.
items.exampleTr: Cumartesi 'meşgul' olduğunu söyledi. Bundan ne anlarsan artık.
items.simple: I tell you the facts; you decide what they mean.
dialogue: A: So she just left without saying goodbye?
B: Yep. Make of that what you will.
items.note: Yorumu karşıya bırakarak ima etmek için.

items.example: What's your take on the new working-from-home rules?
items.exampleTr: Yeni evden çalışma kuralları hakkında ne düşünüyorsun?
items.simple: A way to ask what someone thinks about something.
dialogue: A: What's your take on all this AI stuff?
B: Honestly? Half excited, half terrified.
items.note: 'take' = görüş, yorum. Gündelik, iş ortamında da uygun.

items.example: Here's a hot take: the original film was better.
items.exampleTr: İddialı bir görüş: ilk film daha iyiydi.
items.simple: A bold opinion that many people will not agree with.
dialogue: A: Pineapple on pizza is actually great.
B: Ooh, that's a hot take.
items.note: Sosyal medyadan çıkma; bazen alaycı: 'Wow, what a hot take.'

items.en: There's more to it than meets the eye
items.example: Everyone blames the driver, but there's more to it than meets the eye.
items.exampleTr: Herkes şoförü suçluyor ama işin göründüğünden fazlası var.
items.simple: The story is more complicated than it looks at first.
dialogue: A: Why would a happy couple suddenly split up?
B: I reckon there's more to it than meets the eye.
items.note: Haber ve dedikodularda 'Bu işte bir bit yeniği var' tonu.

items.tr: kaygan zemin, sonu kötü giden yol
items.example: Letting them work weekends once is a slippery slope.
items.exampleTr: Bir kez hafta sonu çalıştırmak kaygan bir zemin.
items.simple: One small step that can lead to more and more bad things.
dialogue: A: It's just one extra hour a day.
B: That's a slippery slope, mate.
items.note: Tartışmalarda: 'It's a slippery slope.'

items.example: I'm calling it now: they'll be engaged by Christmas.
items.exampleTr: Şimdiden söylüyorum: Noel'e kadar nişanlanırlar.
items.simple: You say what will happen before it happens, to show you knew.
dialogue: A: The new guy seems nice.
B: I'm calling it now, he'll be the boss in a year.
items.note: Tahmin yaparken esprili ve kendinden emin.

items.example: Him telling me to save money? That's a bit rich coming from him.
items.exampleTr: Bana para biriktir diyor, onun ağzına yakışıyor mu?
items.simple: Someone criticises you for something they do too.
dialogue: A: Sam says you're always late.
B: That's a bit rich coming from Sam!
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ikiyüzlülüğü belirtirken.

items.example: It's just a rumour online. Don't believe everything you read.
items.exampleTr: İnternette bir söylenti sadece. Okuduğun her şeye inanma.
items.simple: Things you see on the internet or in papers are not always true.
dialogue: A: It says here coffee causes baldness!
B: Don't believe everything you read.
items.note: Sosyal medya haberleri için sık uyarı.

items.example: Mark my words, prices are going up again next year.
items.exampleTr: Bak göreceksin, fiyatlar seneye yine artacak.
items.simple: Remember what I say now, because it will come true.
dialogue: A: Do you think the new café will last?
B: Mark my words, it'll be closed by summer.
items.note: Kehanet tonu; biraz yaşlı ağzı ama çok yaygın.

items.tr: onu tanıdığım kadarıyla, ondan bu beklenir
items.example: Knowing him, he'll turn up an hour late with no apology.
items.exampleTr: Onu bildiğim kadarıyla bir saat geç gelir, özür de dilemez.
items.simple: Because you know what he is like, you can guess what he'll do.
dialogue: A: Do you think he's read the email?
B: Knowing him, he hasn't even opened it.
items.note: Zamir değişir: 'knowing her / knowing my mum'.

items.tr: her şey biraz fazla denk gelmiş
items.example: He lost the files the day before the audit? It's all a bit convenient.
items.exampleTr: Denetimden bir gün önce dosyaları mı kaybetti? Her şey biraz fazla denk gelmiş.
items.simple: Something happens at just the right time for someone, so it seems planned.
dialogue: A: She got sick the day of her presentation.
B: Hmm, all a bit convenient, isn't it?
items.note: Şüphe ima eder: 'Isn't it all a bit convenient?'
